summary: An essay on how Silicon Valley AI boosters, from Marc Andreessen's Techno-Optimist Manifesto to the e/acc movement and the 2024 Consumer Electronics Show, treat artificial intelligence with cult-like faith while pushing to take creative work without consent.

evidence.note: host reports from the Consumer Electronics Show held about a week before recording, January 2024
long segment on Andreessen's manifesto published the previous year, compared with Scientology
AI faith compared at length to Scientology tech and fair game, later to NXIVM
e/acc introduced as the core subculture of the story
Nick Land's racism and gene-editing eugenics, cited in Andreessen's manifesto
Rationalists and LessWrong; Roko's basilisk posted in 2010
Dudesy and the AI-imitation George Carlin special, sued by the Carlin family
AI voice-cloning fraud, including a fake kidnapping call

notes: Format set to current-affairs: an essay adapted from a Rolling Stone article on contemporary AI culture and CES 2024, not a narrative history. No single person anchors it, so the primary subject is the e/acc movement and roles are empty. Covered span starts at Roko's basilisk (2010); the rationalists' early-2000s origins and the late-1990s skeptic movement are mentioned only briefly.
